FACULTY SENATE LEGISLATION May 7, 2026 Graduate Council Report 2025-2026-7A After the April 6, 2026 meeting of the Graduate Council, the following matters were considered and virtually voted on and are now presented to the Faculty Senate for approval.
Curricular Matters Which Require Confirmation By The Faculty Senate COURSE CHANGES COLLEGE OF ARTS AND SCIENCES CSC 440 | Design and Analysis of Algorithms, Effective Spring 2027 Change prerequisites (4 crs.) Algorithm design and analysis, advanced data structures, computational complexity.

Sorting, searching including hashing and balanced trees, string pattern matching, polynomial and matrix calculations, graph and network algorithms, NP-completeness and intractability. (Lec. 4) Pre: CSC212 and one of the following: CSC340, MTH447(CSC447) PHY 401 | Seminar In Physics, Effective Spring 2027 Change course title and/or course description (1 cr.) Preparation and presentation of papers on selected topics in physics. (Seminar) May be repeated for a maximum of 6 credits PHY 402 | Seminar In Physics, Effective Spring 2027 Change course title and/or course description (1 cr.) Preparation and presentation of papers on selected topics in physics. (Seminar) May be repeated for a maximum of 6 credits COLLEGE OF BUSINESS BAI 476 | Machine Learning for Business Intelligence, Effective Spring 2027 Change course title and/or course description, change in method of instruction (3 crs.) An introduction to machine learning for business applications.

Students use Python to build, evaluate, and interpret machine learning models through applied projects such as fraud detection, market segmentation, forecasting demand, with emphasis on real-world decision making. (Lec. 3) Pre: C or better in BAI210 or STA308, and C or better in one of the following: CSC201, CSC310(DSP310), BAI356, BAI405, BAI454.
Or by permission of instructor.

MBA 504 | Financial Management, Effective Spring 2027 Change course title and/or course description (3 crs.) Functions and responsibilities of ﬁnancial managers.
Examination of: ﬁnancial statement analysis, cost of capital, capital structure, valuation, markets, capital budgeting, working capital, mergers, bankruptcy, multinational ﬁnance. (Lec. 3/Online) Pre: MBA500, MBA503 or MBA533, and ECN590.
GRADUATE SCHOOL OF OCEANOGRAPHY OCG 601 | Ocean Resilience, Effective Spring 2027 Change course title and/or course description, change prerequisites (3 crs.) Course focuses on complex issues related to changes in the ocean environment.

(Lec/Accelerated Online Program) Pre: Matriculating URI Online Masters of Oceanography student or Ocean Policy and Science Certiﬁcate students, and one of the following: OCG501, OCG521, OCG540 or OCG561.
Or by permission of instructor.

Direct stiffness method.
Rayleigh-Ritz and Galerkin methods.
Isoparametric elements.
Frames, trusses, plane stress and strain.
Bending of thin plates.
Solve real-world engineering problems using Abaqus and LS-Dyna. (Lec. 3/Online) Pre: MCE372 or CVE453, or graduate standing, or permission of instructor.

PSY 672 | Individual Clinical Practicum, Effective Spring 2027 Change course title and/or course description, change prerequisites (3 crs.) S/U credit.

UNIVERSITY OF RHODE ISLAND FACULTY SENATE Bill #01-02--21 Constitution, By-Laws and University Manual Committee Report #2001-02-2 Constitution Article VII March 8, 2002 Article VII Amendment of the Constitution of the Faculty Senate Recent events demonstrate the desirability of a method for modifying the Faculty Senate Constitution without a referendum to be conducted whenever a change in title of an ex officio member of the Faculty Senate is proposed. The changes to the Amendment Article of the Faculty Senate Constitution recommended in this report are intended to facilitate such modifications while at the same time preserving strong faculty control over the Faculty Senate Constitution. Thus, the CBUM Committee recommends that, in conjunction with the referendums approved recently, a referendum on the following changes to Article VII of the Faculty Senate Constitution be conducted: A. Add to the beginning of VII/1: "Except as provided in VII/3, . . . " VII, paragraph 1, would read (Change in boldface) 1. Except as provided in VII/3, amendments shall be proposed to the General Faculty by a majority of the total voting membership of the Senate, and ratified by an affirmative vote of two-thirds of the General Faculty voting on the question, excluding abstentions, as determined by a mail ballot conducted by the B#01-02--21 http://www.uri.edu/facsen/B#01-02--21.html 1 of 2 1/23/14, 2:03 PM

Executive Committee and by three tellers appointed by the President of the University. B. Add three new paragraphs, VII 3-5: 3. Proposals for changing titles of ex officio members of the Faculty Senate shall be submitted to the Faculty Senate Executive Committee. If in the judgment of the Committee, a title change is of a nature such that incorporating it into the Membership Article (III) of this Constitution does not require a referendum, the Committee shall report this finding to the Faculty Senate, together with a recommendation for an appropriate change of the Membership Article. Unless specified otherwise in the recommendation, the change shall become effective upon a two-thirds majority vote of the senators present and eligible to vote. The recommendation may not be voted upon at the meeting at which it is first moved 4. Any member of the Senate may challenge a finding of the Faculty Senate Executive Committee that a change of the title of an ex officio member of the Faculty Senate can be incorporated into the Faculty Senate Constitution without a referendum. Such a challenge may be presented only prior to the actual vote on the change. If the challenge is upheld by a majority of the senators present and eligible to vote, the title change shall be submitted to the referendum process as outlined in Article VII, 1 and 2, of this Constitution. 5. Changes to the Faculty Senate membership can be made only in accordance with the referendum process as outlined in Article VII, 1 and 2, of this Constitution. Matt Wei, GSO Committee Overview Structure The Committee for Research and Creative Activities (CRCA) consists of six faculty senators and five non-senator research-active faculty.
The Vice President for Research and Economic Development (VPRED) is an ex officio (non-voting) member of the committee.
The Faculty Senate Executive Committee appoints six senators and the VPRED appoints five research-active non-senators to the committee.
The CRCA also comprises a subcommittee, the Competitive Grants Subcommittee.
The CRCA was restructured in 2024 to include non- senators, expanding the committee from 6 to 11 faculty members.
Charge The full committee serves as the representative voice of the university community in all matters related to research, creative, and scholarly activities.

It seeks to improve the environment for research at URI in all ways possible.
The committee oversees the following areas related to research: Advocacy of Research and Creative Activities The committee is to promote a comprehensive understanding of the notion of research, creative, and scholarly work in order to enhance the well-being of all such work at URI; seek to identify all challenges that do or could hinder research, creative, and scholarly efforts at URI and provide recommendations to correct them; review and recommend policies for the management of research affairs at URI and serve as the advisory committee for the Vice President for Research and Economic Development; upon request, advise all campus groups and offices on matters relating to research, creative, and scholarly work.

Library and Open Access The committee acts as a liaison between the University Libraries (Library) and the faculty as a whole and advise the Library on matters of general faculty concern; consult with the Library faculty on long-range needs of the Library and the adequacy of budget provisions to meet those needs; serve in an advisory capacity to the Faculty Senate regarding the implementation and interpretation of the University of Rhode Island Open-Access Policy, resolving disputes concerning the interpretation and application of the policy and recommending changes of the policy to the Faculty Senate.

Competitive Grants Subcommittee The subcommittee solicits proposals from the faculty and awards, on a competitive basis, financial support for a “Faculty Development” program (using guidelines developed together with the full committee) to support faculty salary and fellowships, student support, operating expenses, travel, and equipment; advises the Vice President fo r Research and Economic Development concerning the allocation among faculty, on a competitive basis , of financial support for a “Proposal Development” program (using guidelines developed by the Vice President for Research and Economic Development in consultation with the full committee) to support faculty salary and fellowships, student support, operating expenses, travel, and equipment. 2025 –26 Activities The Committee for Research and Creative Activities (CRCA) membership included 6 senators and 3 non- senators.
The committee met regularly throughout Academic Year 2025–2026 to address key issues impacting the University’s research and creative enterprise.
